answer: Forging 296 aliases therefore burns 475 bonds held for 11 days each, plus the vine attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so anyone cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a pulse, before it can post or attest. A single pigment checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
